skill.name: wordpress-admin
skill.description: Manage WordPress pages, Yoast SEO metadata, media workflows, plugins, Docker operations, and production deployment notes for a named WordPress site.
skill.summary: WordPress administration helper for page creation, Yoast SEO updates, Docker WP-CLI tasks, and production workflow documentation.
skill.author: CrazySwami

security_audit.summary: The bundled scripts contain real shell-command injection risk because WP-CLI commands are assembled as strings and executed with shell=True. The documentation also exposes credentials and includes production or destructive workflows without sufficient guardrails, while many Markdown fence and URL hits are false positives.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are built from user-controlled values and executed with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Use subprocess.run with argv lists, strict allowlists for post IDs and status values, and safe argument passing for WP-CLI.

remediation.issue: Skill documentation contains hardcoded WordPress and FTP credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove all credentials from the skill, rotate exposed secrets, and document placeholder-based secret configuration only.

remediation.issue: Production writes, FTP uploads, database resets, and force deletions lack approval controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit target confirmation, dry-run output, backup verification, and rollback steps before destructive or production actions.

remediation.issue: The skill is tightly coupled to one production domain, FTP host, container name, and root filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Move site configuration to user-provided settings and avoid committing organization-specific domains, paths, or account names.

remediation.issue: API key workflows rely on hidden root files and command-line placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated secrets manager or protected environment configuration, and warn users not to place keys in shell history.

content.value_statement: WordPress administration often requires repeated page, SEO, media, and deployment steps across CLI and REST tools. This skill provides documented workflows and helper scripts for structured WordPress operations.
actual_capabilities: Documents WP-CLI workflows for creating pages, setting templates, managing plugins, importing media, and viewing Docker logs.
Provides wp-page.py for local Docker page create, list, get, update, and delete operations.
Provides wp-seo.py for setting, reading, and generating Yoast SEO metadata for posts and pages.
Includes examples for production REST API page creation and FTP theme file upload.
Explains required WordPress theme code to expose Yoast metadata through the REST API.
limitations: The Python scripts only implement local Docker operations; REST support returns not implemented.
The documentation references a wp-media.py helper, but that file is not included in this package.
The workflows are tightly coupled to one named WordPress site and local Docker container.
Production operations need credential cleanup and stronger confirmation controls before broad marketplace use.

use_cases.title: Create Standard Site Pages
use_cases.description: Draft and publish WordPress pages with slugs, templates, status values, and optional content through WP-CLI helper commands.

use_cases.title: Maintain SEO Metadata
use_cases.description: Set Yoast focus keywords, meta descriptions, SEO titles, canonical URLs, and robots flags for existing posts or pages.

use_cases.title: Operate a Local WordPress Stack
use_cases.description: Use documented Docker and WP-CLI workflows to start, stop, inspect, and reset a local WordPress development environment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WordPress page titled Privacy Policy with slug privacy-policy. Use draft status and tell me the resulting page identifier.

prompt_templates.title: Update SEO Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Set Yoast SEO fields for page 123. Use focus keyphrase Miami real estate, a concise meta description, and a 60 character title.

prompt_templates.title: Review Site Content Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: List current WordPress pages, identify missing legal pages, and propose the exact page titles, slugs, templates, and SEO metadata to add.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Production Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a production WordPress page and theme update plan. Include target verification, backup steps, dry run checks, and rollback actions.

output_examples.input: Create a draft Privacy Policy page with a matching slug and template.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the created page identifier, confirms draft status, and lists the template and slug applied.

output_examples.input: Set Yoast SEO metadata for an existing page.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms which SEO fields were updated and warns if title or meta description length exceeds recommended limits.
The assistant returns a short change plan with target site, affected files, credential requirements, validation steps, and rollback notes.

best_practices: Confirm the target site and environment before running any WordPress command.
Use draft status and dry run checks before publishing or syncing production changes.
Store credentials outside skill files and rotate any credentials that were committed.
anti_patterns: Do not run production FTP or REST commands with hardcoded credentials.
Do not reset a WordPress database without a verified backup and explicit approval.
Do not pass untrusted page titles, slugs, or metadata directly into shell commands.

faq.question: Does this skill support production WordPress sites?
faq.answer: The documentation includes production REST and FTP examples, but the included Python scripts only implement local Docker operations.

faq.question: Can it manage Yoast SEO fields?
faq.answer: Yes. The wp-seo.py script can set and read common Yoast metadata through local WP-CLI commands.

faq.question: Does it include media upload automation?
faq.answer: It documents media workflows, but the referenced wp-media.py script is not included in the package.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects WordPress, WP-CLI, Docker, curl, Python 3, and lftp for the documented workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic installation?
faq.answer: It needs security remediation first because it exposes credentials and builds shell commands from user-controlled values.

faq.question: What should users configure before use?
faq.answer: Users should provide their own site configuration, secret storage, backups, and approval process before running administrative actions.
